title: Login validation
idea: `userLoginValidator` is the short rule list in front of the login controller. It checks only that a real-looking email and a text password arrived.
points: Login rules ask for less than register rules: an email and a text password.
Strength rules stay in registration, so passwords set under older rules still work.
Bad shape gets `422` from `validate`; wrong credentials get `401` from the controller.
Test every branch: empty body, bad types, unknown email, wrong password, success.

steps.caption: A client posts an empty body `{}` to `/login`. The rules run first.
Both fields fail. The rules record two errors and call `next()`; they reject nothing themselves.
`validate` finds recorded errors and throws `ApiError(422)`. The controller and the database are never reached.
The client gets `422` and one message per field. Nothing was queried.
A second body is well formed, with an email and a password. The rules record nothing.
`validate` finds no errors and calls `next()`. Now the database gets involved.
The controller looks up the user and compares the password with the stored hash. They differ.
It throws `ApiError(401)`. An unknown email gets the same answer, so the reply never says which emails exist.
A third body has the right password. It passes the rules and `validate`, and the controller accepts it.
The controller answers `200`. Setting the token cookies happens here, as in the last lesson.

code.title: Login rules, tested
code.caption: The new validator sits among condensed earlier files. Press Run: six requests, three kinds of answer.

walk.text: Condensed from earlier lessons: `ApiError`, a two-field `User` and `validate`.
Two rules per field. `bail()` stops a field at its first failure.
`isString` rejects objects and numbers, which `bcrypt.compare` cannot handle.
The controller runs only for valid input. Both failures share one `401` message.
Rules, then `validate`, then the controller: route order is run order.
Connect and seed one user; only a bcrypt hash is stored.
Six requests: three fail validation, two fail credentials, one succeeds.

pitfalls: Do not copy register's strength rules into login: older passwords would stop working.
Require a text password: `bcrypt.compare` throws on a number, which becomes a `500`.
Never `trim()` or change the password: it must match what was hashed.

quiz.why: `isString` fails for a number, so `validate` throws `422`. The controller and `bcrypt.compare` never run.

takeaway: Validate the shape at the door; check the credentials in the controller.

starters: What is the difference between a 422 and a 401 on login?
Why should login not check password strength?
How do I send these same bodies from Postman?
